open_points.subject: Agent authorization
open_points.text: “the token says whether the agent may author” conflicts with the action table, which says “agent with author right” for functions and trial cases but only “agent” for “propose an operation binding” and “compose and prove a flow”
open_points.question: Does the may-author right also govern composing flow versions and proposing operation bindings, or are those actions available to every authenticated agent?
options: May-author is required only where the action table explicitly says so
May-author is required for every action that creates authored records, including flows and binding proposals
May-author is required for flow composition but not binding proposals, or vice versa
open_points.default_guess: Require may-author only for actions explicitly marked “agent with author right”; allow every agent to compose flows and propose bindings.

open_points.subject: ContractVersion corpus, AdmissionVerdict and Activation
open_points.text: “activation, which requires an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus” and “the corpus only grows” do not say what happens to an existing activation when a trial case is added and its verdict no longer covers the current corpus
open_points.question: After the corpus grows, is the previously active implementation still runnable, automatically re-admitted, or no longer a usable current activation until a new admission succeeds?
options: Keep the activation and continue allowing runs
Keep the historical activation record but refuse new runs until an implementation is admitted over the enlarged corpus
Automatically re-run admission for the active implementation
Remove or supersede the current activation when the corpus grows
open_points.default_guess: Keep the activation as history but treat it as unusable for new runs until an implementation receives an admitted verdict over the enlarged corpus.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution
open_points.text: M07 records `implementation_id`, `trial_case_id`, outcome and time, but no actor or reason for execution, even though executions are created both by an agent's “try an implementation” action and by the kernel during admission, while K-15 says “The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record.”
open_points.question: What fact distinguishes an agent-requested trial execution from a kernel-run admission execution, and which agent requested an explicit trial?
options: Store an initiating actor and an execution purpose such as `trial` or `admission` on TrialExecution
Link each TrialExecution to a separate request or admission record that carries the actor and purpose
Do not retain this provenance despite K-15
open_points.default_guess: Store both the initiating actor and whether the execution was an explicit trial or part of admission.

open_points.subject: ProofResult
open_points.text: M17 says “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result,” while M14 says proof refuses an unaccepted binding and the carried-to-State-2 text says a version that failed for that reason “can be proven again later” after acceptance
open_points.question: What is the identity and meaning of a ProofResult when mutable binding status can make the same flow version produce different results at different times?
options: ProofResult is an invocation-time value whose facts include or are scoped by the binding state used
ProofResult is only a transient response with no stable identity claim
ProofResult is keyed only by flow_version_id and is replaced when dependencies change
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a transient invocation-time result and do not claim that a flow version alone determines it.

open_points.subject: Read-only FlowActivation
open_points.text: M18 says read-only activation is performed by “the kernel” and carries only `activated_by`, while State 0 says an owner or agent must ask for that activation and K-15 requires their actions to remain distinguishable
open_points.question: Where is the owner or agent who requested a kernel-performed read-only activation recorded?
options: Add a requesting actor distinct from `activated_by`, which remains `kernel`
Set `activated_by` to the requester even though the kernel performs the automatic step
Record a separate activation request
Do not retain the requester
open_points.default_guess: Record the requester separately and keep `activated_by` as `kernel` for the automatic activation.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution
open_points.text: M23 classifies NodeExecution as `Identity: value` but also says “an attempt's record is issued once,” identifies it by `run_id`, `node_id`, `map_index`, `attempt_number`, and is referenced by that identity from TrialCase; M07 classifies the analogous issued execution observation as an entity
open_points.question: Is a NodeExecution an entity identified by its attempt coordinates, or a content-derived value subject to value equality and deduplication?
options: An entity with the attempt-coordinate tuple as its stable identity
An entity with an additional kernel-minted identifier
A content-derived value that can be substituted or deduplicated when all facts match
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an immutable entity identified by `(run_id, node_id, map_index, attempt_number)`.
